# The Friday close

Do these jobs in order. Each one writes new files in out/ and changes no original file.
Read CLAUDE.md and notes/owner-notes.md first.

## Steps

1. **Say what is here.** Write out/whats-here.md: one line for each top-level folder (orders, customers, prices,
   invoices, purchase-orders, recipes, allergens, labels, menu, till, notes, out) saying what it holds. End with a
   heading "## Questions I have" and at least two questions as dash lines.
2. **Clean the orders.** Read orders/wholesale-orders.csv. Write out/orders-clean.csv with exactly the columns
   order_id, order_date, cafe, product, quantity. Dates as YYYY-MM-DD (phone orders are day first). Cafe names
   exactly as in customers/cafes.csv. Quantities as whole numbers. Drop a row only when it is an exact copy of
   another row.
3. **Fix the price list.** Read prices/price-list.xlsx. Product names must match the first line of each recipe.
   Every price in pounds, as a number, for one item (unit "each"). Write out/price-list-clean.xlsx with the
   columns product, unit, shop_price, wholesale_price, and out/price-changes.md with one dash line for each
   product you changed and no others.
4. **Check the invoices.** Compare every PDF in invoices/ with purchase-orders/purchase-orders.csv. Write
   out/reconciliation.csv with the columns invoice, po, status, reason, one row for every invoice. Status is "ok"
   when it matches. Otherwise use "duplicate", "price above PO" or "short delivery". Then write
   out/reconciliation-note.md: what needs action, in under 150 words.
5. **Make the labels.** Use the allergen-label skill for every recipe.
6. **Write the report.** Use the monday-report skill.
7. **Update the menu page.** Write out/site/index.html: every product on the clean price list, its shop price
   and its allergens from its label. One file, no script from another site, readable on a phone.

## Never

- Never change, move or delete an original file.
- Never sign a label. A person does that.
- Never guess a number. Every number comes from a file in this folder.

When you finish, list each file you made.

description: Make the shelf label for a Wren Street Bakery product from its recipe, with its price and every allergen. Use when asked for a label, or for allergens on a product.

# Allergen label

## Steps

1. Read the recipe in recipes/. The product name is its first line.
2. Read allergens/allergen-list.csv. An allergen is in the product when any of its look_for words is in the
   recipe's Ingredients part. Read every ingredient, including the words in brackets.
3. Find the shop price for the product in out/price-list-clean.xlsx.
4. Write out/labels/<the recipe file name>, in this shape:

```text
# <Product name>

Price: £<price, two decimals>

Contains: <allergens, lower case, comma separated, in the order of allergen-list.csv>

Checked by:
```

## Never

- Never fill in "Checked by:". A person reads the label and signs it.
- Never leave out an allergen because the old label in labels/ does not have it. The recipe is the truth.
- Never write to labels/. New labels go in out/labels/.
---
name: monday-report
description: Write the Monday report for Wren Street Bakery from the till. Use when asked for the Monday report, sales, waste or who pays late.
---

# The Monday report

## Steps

1. Read till/sales.csv. Add up takings, items sold and items wasted over every row. Find the product with
   the most waste.
2. Read notes/owner-notes.md for the cafes that pay late.
3. Write out/reports/monday-report.md with a two sentence summary at the top, then these headings:
   "## Sales" (takings in pounds and items sold), "## Waste" (items wasted, and the product with the most
   waste and its count) and "## Late payers" (one dash line per cafe).

## Never

- Never round a total you did not add up. Work the numbers out with a script, not in your head.
- Never change till/sales.csv.

# Wren Street Bakery

This is the bakery's shared folder. It is made-up data for practice.

| Folder | What is in it |
|---|---|
| orders/ | Cafe orders, exported from three places |
| customers/ | The six cafes we deliver to |
| prices/ | The price list |
| invoices/ | Supplier invoices as PDFs |
| purchase-orders/ | What we ordered from suppliers |
| recipes/ | One recipe for each product |
| allergens/ | The words we look for in recipes |
| labels/ | The labels on the shop shelf |
| menu/ | The menu on the shop wall |
| till/ | What sold, from the till |
| notes/ | Notes from Jess, the owner |
| out/ | Put new files here |
# How I keep the bakery folder safe

I work in Manual mode.

## Claude will ask me before

- it changes or makes a file
- it runs a command
I want Claude to match our delivery notes to the orders so I stop doing it by hand.
# The till

The till writes `sales.csv` at closing time. One row for each product on each day the shop is open.

Nobody edits this file by hand. It is the record of what really sold.

==> recipes/almond-croissant.md <==
# Almond Croissant

## Ingredients

- croissant (wheat flour, butter, milk, egg)
- almonds
- sugar
- egg
